summary: Biraja Sankar Guha worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Scottish Church College, University of Calcutta, and Harvard University. His career included posts at the University of Calcutta, the Zoological Survey of India, and the Ethnographic Survey of India.

Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura and studied under Muni Jambūvijaya. She held positions at Heidelberg University, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Bo Jiang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University between roughly 2002 and 2008 under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bokar Rinpoche was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche and later held a post at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery from around 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, Jacqueline I. Stone, Yang Lu, Chun-fang Yu, Lewis Lancaster, and Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh.

Bongkil Chung worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and later served as professor of philosophy at Florida International University from 1991 to 1992.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was an expert in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky from around 1921 to 1925 and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from approximately 1930 to 1934.

Borjigidai Oyunbilig specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held a post in Mongolian studies at the University of Bonn (~1999–2001) and became a professor at Renmin University of China around 2008.
Brad Warner is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He attended Wadsworth High School and Kent State University, and studied under Tim McCarthy (~1983–1993) and Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1994).

Bradford Lyman Phillips works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Naropa University, Harvard University, and the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano alongside mentors such as Michael Aris, Masatoshi Nagatomi, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College around 2006.

Braj Basi Lal worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at the University of Allahabad. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972), a professor at Jiwaji University (1972), and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a PhD at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and his habilitation at LMU Munich. His career includes posts at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, SOAS, and LMU Munich.
Brandon J. Harwood is a religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Louisville between roughly 2009 and 2015, where he studied under the supervision of Patrick Pranke.

Brendan S. Gillon specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from around 1979 to 1984 and later served as Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, he held posts at Shiga University, Kwansei Gakuin University, Otani University, Kyoto University, and Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds between roughly 1978 and 1984, where he studied under Michael Pye.

Brian D. Ruppert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, and was mentored by Willis Stoesz. He held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2016) before joining Bates College around 2016.

Brian Daizen Victoria is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple University. He held academic posts at the University of Adelaide (~1997–2002) and Antioch University (~2003–2005).

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University (~2000–2006) under György Kara, Christopher P. Atwood, Christopher I. Beckwith, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and Elliot Sperling.
